name: Data centre siting and power procurement
aliases: Hyperscale data centre siting and power procurement
principle: Siting is the data centre's first and most binding engineering decision: power availability, price and time-to-energisation outrank almost everything else, followed by water, fibre and latency. The 2025 boom in behind-the-meter generation (about 46 projects, about 56 GW self-planned, ~90% announced in 2025) exists because grid interconnection queues cannot keep pace; operators therefore choose between grid feed, behind-the-meter gas, PPAs for advanced nuclear or fuel cells, and hybrids — and in Southeast Asia the Johor-Cyberjaya corridor has become the fastest-growing supply region, with AirTrunk's Malaysia platform alone expanding past 700 MW.

process_steps.name: Screen regions on power, water, fibre, latency and policy
Choose and contract the power route

limitations: Grid queues and turbine backlogs move lead times beyond typical build schedules
Water availability increasingly constrains cooling choices
Jurisdiction policy ( Singapore's DC-CFA caps, moratoria elsewhere) shapes the map
